article.title: Why Trimming Extreme Propensity Scores Changes the Question You Are Answering
article.why: Understand that trimming can improve stability while changing the target population and estimand.
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

sources.label: Background: propensity scores and causal inference

paragraphs.en:
Propensity-score methods try to make treated and untreated groups more comparable using observed covariates. But sometimes the two groups barely overlap. A customer with a propensity score of 0.99 has almost no comparable untreated counterpart, while a customer with a score of 0.01 has almost no comparable treated counterpart. Weighting such observations can create very large weights and unstable estimates.

One common response is trimming: remove observations with extreme propensity scores and estimate the effect in the region where treated and control units have better overlap. This can reduce variance, limit the influence of a few observations, and improve the practical credibility of the comparison. Yet trimming is not merely a technical cleanup step. It can change the population about which the analysis makes a claim.

Consider a campaign offered mainly to high-value customers. Customers with extremely high predicted treatment probability may be almost always treated. If analysts remove them because there are too few comparable controls, the resulting estimate no longer describes all eligible customers. It describes a more restricted group for whom treatment assignment was realistically uncertain. That may be a sensible target, but it is a different target.

This is where the idea of an estimand matters. An estimand defines the causal quantity we want to estimate: for example, the average treatment effect for the whole population, the effect among treated customers, or the effect in an overlap population. A statistical procedure is not complete until we know which estimand its result represents.

Suppose the original business question is, ‘What would happen if we sent this offer to every eligible customer?’ If trimming removes the highest-value 15 percent and the lowest-propensity 10 percent, the remaining estimate cannot automatically answer that original question. It may answer, ‘What is the effect among customers who had a reasonable chance of receiving either treatment?’ Extrapolating from that group back to everyone requires additional assumptions.

Analysts should therefore document the trimming rule before looking at the outcome when possible. They should report how many observations were removed, which types of customers were disproportionately excluded, how the propensity-score distributions changed, and how effective sample size and weight distributions changed. Sensitivity analyses using alternative thresholds can show whether the conclusion depends heavily on one arbitrary cutoff.

There is also a business interpretation. Extreme scores often reveal a policy boundary. If some customers are almost guaranteed to receive treatment because of operational rules, the data contain little natural information about what would have happened to similar untreated customers. The problem is not solved simply by a more sophisticated model. It reflects limited support in the observed decision process.

Trimming can be the right choice. The mistake is to present the post-trimming estimate as if nothing about the question changed. A more transparent conclusion is: ‘After restricting the analysis to customers with sufficient overlap, we estimate an effect of X for that overlap population.’ Statistical stability and population relevance are both important, and improving one can narrow the other.
paragraphs.zh: Trimming 極端 propensity score 可以減少 extreme weights、改善穩定性，但它同時排除了某些人，因此估計結果適用的 target population 也可能改變。關鍵概念是 estimand：你究竟估計全體 ATE、treated 的 ATT，還是 overlap population 的效果。報告 trimming 時應說明門檻、排除比例、被排除者特徵、ESS 與敏感度分析。
paragraphs.ja: 極端な傾向スコアをtrimすると、巨大なweightを抑えて推定を安定させやすくなります。しかし除外された人は推定対象から外れるため、結果が答える『誰への効果か』も変わり得ます。estimandを明示し、除外割合・対象属性・ESS・閾値感度を報告することが重要です。

quiz.question: Why is trimming not just technical cleanup?
quiz.answer: Because removing extreme-score observations can change the population and estimand to which the causal estimate applies.
